chapter: Freelancing, Miller and the girls' bands
title: Sweethearts personnel and their wealthy backer
summary: Vi Burnside was the tenor star; a rich Washington backer funded two bands, sleeper buses and big acts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Who were the girls -- what was the girl in that band who was a tenor player in that band that was very good.
Named Vy Burnside.
Hm?
Named Vy Burnside.
Ah, that's right, yeah.
She died.
Died?
About six, seven years ago. But there
was another girl I had in the other band, because I had to organize another band from the same man that owned the Sweethearts, to make money, and use the two bands.
And this girl named Lilly Labourney, she there now, and she's as great as any man you ever want to hear in your life.
Wasn't there somebody named Anna Mae Winbone or something?
She came in and took over the band when I left.
Oh, I see.
But they could never get me back over there. I wouldn't go back, see, because there was a lot of work that I would never do again.
Well, I was going to ask you, didn't you have a lot of headaches with girls?

I didn't have any headaches with the girls, because they did what I said and they asked no questions. But the point was, the only reason I was successful with this band is because they had unlimited money from the backer.
Who was the backer? Was that Irving Mills?
No, it was a Western fellow in Washington, D.C., kept a half a million standing in the banks. Money was no problem. We bought that All-American sleeper and then I
bought another sleeper bus for the other band, had it made. That's the kind of money, man, it was. We all know Arlington Cemetery. He gave that land to the government and a lot of things like that.

He's dead, now. So I brought him up to meet Gail and he put all the money up. And that's the only way we got by the band, because I was paying $1,000 in those days, $2,000 worth of gals, with all that help. And then Ella was with the band a lot, and we got acts like Buddy Beans and Susan, Ella Fitzgerald on the same program. Had top acts with the band.
Oh, yeah?
That helped with those big names, and that band could play, too, because I trained them.
